scope: Isolated S1 frame containment paths and a split scope run. The multiprocess scope run had used about 57 of its 80-second fixture deadline in one engine process. The runner now runs the scope cases in three parts, each in its own engine process: documents (51 cases), frames (8 cases), and processes (28 cases, multiprocess only). Three shared cases and six multiprocess cases check a frame's first navigation, a failed frame with a healthy pending navigation, and frame history after a contained failure. The engine patch does not change. No product dependency or runtime configuration changes.
owner_decisions: A child frame's failure must stay inside that frame. A healthy parent in another event loop keeps its document and its scope. Only the failed frame shows an error state. This applies to an active frame and to a frame whose navigation is pending (2026-11-26).

baseline.head: b4318a2
baseline.note: The JavaScript URL crash evidence records three passing runs in each mode at b4318a2. origin/main was at b4318a2 when this work started.

configuration.part_check: Each part runs as its own fixture process, for example --document-scope-multiprocess frames. Each part must print exactly its own case markers, ending with its summary marker, and the summary must report its own case count. Each repeat must then cover 59 cases in single-process mode or 87 cases in multiprocess mode, each once. The frames and processes parts start a fresh view at the fixture origin and check it as the independent view.
configuration.frame_path_check: Each frame path case holds the healthy parent's script thread at a barrier and queues eight mixed callbacks there. Inside the barrier, the host waits until the frame state probe shows the failed pipeline handled: for a first navigation, the initial about:blank pipeline still current and live with no pending pipeline; otherwise, the failed current pipeline gone with no pending pipeline. A revocation or crash notification of the parent also ends the wait. The parent must have no terminal callback, no revocation, and no crash notification. After release, all eight callbacks succeed in the parent's document, its retained reply passes, and the probe reports a new live frame pipeline whose crash details begin with the exact reason.
configuration.frame_view_check: The parent reads its frame's last posted path, the frame element's load event count, history.length, and the frame's URL or the cross-origin error. A second intercepted site, https://frame-site.invalid, serves cross-site children that post their path to the parent. These page values only order the fixture and grant no host authority.

engine_patch.change: None. The three frame paths pass with the patch at b4318a2.

fixture_changes: run() now takes a required part: documents, frames, or processes. The processes part requires multiprocess mode.
The frame cases and the multiprocess-only cases moved into frame_cases and process_cases without assertion changes. Their independent view is now a fresh view at the fixture origin.
The runner checks each part's markers and summary count, records each repeat's total, and fails a repeat that does not cover every case of its mode once.
frame_path_failure adds the three frame paths in both modes.
findings: Servo creates a frame's browsing context with an initial about:blank pipeline in the parent's event loop, before the frame's first navigation. The first navigation is therefore an ordinary pending change of an existing browsing context. The skip in contained_failed_frames for a pending pipeline that creates a new browsing context applies only to that about:blank pipeline, which always runs in the parent's event loop.

First navigation: the parent reported DOM readiness, and its load event waited for the frame. The failure closed the pending pipeline, and about:blank stayed current inside the barrier. The error page then replaced about:blank, the frame element fired one load event, and the parent's load completed. history.length stayed 1. A late response reached no document. Reload made the first navigation wait again, and a new URL recovered.

Healthy pending navigation: the patch closed the healthy pending pipeline in the third event loop. Inside the barrier, the probe reported no live current pipeline and no pending pipeline. The error page replaced the child, the frame element fired its second load event, and history.length stayed 1. The late navigation response reached no document and sent no message to the parent. No crash notification and no engine error followed. Reload and a new URL recovered.

Frame history: the error page replaced the failed second child's history entry, and history.length stayed 2. Back rebuilt the first child in a new pipeline that differs from its original pipeline and from the error page. Forward restored the same error page pipeline with its crash details. The parent kept its identity, activation generation, and scope through both traversals. A top-level navigation and back restored the parent with a fresh identity and the same error page, with history.length 3.
A frame document that history rebuilds posts its message, but the frame element fires no load event for it. iframe_load_event_steps ignores a load from a pipeline that the element did not start.

In multiprocess mode, each failed pipeline's process differs from the host's, the parent's, and the independent view's. The healthy pending pipeline runs in a third process. The error page runs in a new process. The rebuilt first child runs outside the failed process.
The behavior is the same in both modes, and for script-thread unwind, child exit, and host SIGKILL.

timing_observations.note: The multiprocess scope cases had run in one engine process for about 57 of its 80 fixture seconds. Each part now runs in its own process. In multiprocess mode, the documents part took 34.1 seconds, the frames part 21.2 seconds, and the processes part 14.9 seconds. Their margins to the 80-second fixture deadline are about 46, 59, and 65 seconds. In single-process mode, the documents part took 6.2 to 9.0 seconds and the frames part 6.9 to 7.0 seconds, within the 30-second fixture deadline. This checkpoint keeps the 80-second and 30-second fixture deadlines and the 90-second and 35-second runner deadlines.

negative_controls.variation: The final patch without the loop in contained_failed_frames that closes a failed frame's other pending pipelines. This is an isolation control for existing code. The fixture is final.
negative_controls.observed_failure: In both modes, frame-healthy-pending-navigation-failure fails inside the barrier: "The frame script-thread unwind was not handled within the barrier: E4 process deadline exceeded; frame=Some(((27,4), false, None, true))". The probe still reports a pending pipeline for the frame after the 4-second barrier wait. In multiprocess mode, frame-healthy-pending-process-exit fails in the same way.
negative_controls.interpretation: All 51 documents cases and the first six frames cases pass in each mode, including frame-initial-navigation-failure. The processes part passes 22 earlier cases and frame-initial-navigation-process-exit. Later cases in a failed part do not run. The healthy pending cases therefore depend on the loop that closes a failed frame's other pending pipelines. Both backend loss cases and both Servo controls pass.

single.scope: Experimental engine scope, host allocation gate, script-thread unwind, final-handle release, explicit engine shutdown, queued execution cancellation, interruption of running JavaScript, content-process exit and forced kill in multiprocess mode, shared-process view revocation and ordinary sibling close, script-thread failure and content-process exit or kill before document construction, crash recovery through reload and history, script-thread failure after response headers and in about:blank, srcdoc, document.write, and document.open() construction, crash recovery of a javascript: URL document to an error page without its result, script-thread failure while a cross-site navigation, a cross-site subframe, or a sandboxed srcdoc child parses in its own event loop, content-process exit or kill while a cross-site document, a cross-site subframe, or a sandboxed srcdoc child parses, script-thread failure and content-process exit or kill while a same-site or cross-site child frame's navigation waits for its response headers, containment of a child frame's failure to that frame when the parent's own top-level document runs in another event loop, including a frame's first navigation, a failed frame with a healthy pending navigation, and frame history after a contained failure, callback and delegate unwind safety, and constellation loss in a separate engine.
